channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Ukraine to possess long-range ballistic missile by autumn, says Zelensky
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will have its own long-range ballistic missile by autumn. He has urged the missile developer, Fire Point, to accelerate work on the FP-9 missile, which is expected to be ready this fall. Zelensky previously reported the first combat use of the FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in October.

item.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Previously Detained for Extremist Materials, Investigated for Attempted Crash
item.description: The co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv, identified as Hamam Al-Hammami, was previously detained in 2024 for possessing extremist materials while training with Oman Air. He was suspended from flying for a year but continued in an administrative role. Investigators are determining how he regained flight privileges.

item.title: Afghanistan and Tajikistan Sign Electricity Supply Agreement for Badakhshan Province
item.description: Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS) and Tajikistan's Pamir Energy Company have signed a cooperation agreement to supply electricity to border districts of Afghanistan's Badakhshan province. The deal, signed in Dushanbe, aims to expand cooperation and improve power services for residents. Discussions also included extending a 110-kilovolt power transmission line to Faizabad.

item.title: United Front reports two attacks against Taliban in Helmand
item.description: The United Front reported two attacks targeting the Taliban in central Helmand. Details regarding the attacks were not immediately available.

item.title: Afghan envoy in Moscow stresses economic cooperation with region
item.description: Afghanistan's ambassador to Moscow, Gul Hassan Hassan, emphasized mutual respect, dialogue, and economic cooperation between Afghanistan and regional countries at an international forum. He spoke at "The North Caucasus: A Space of Dialogue, Traditions and Development."

item.title: Astana residents warned of road restrictions on October 5-6 due to state visit
item.description: Astana residents are advised of temporary road restrictions on October 5-6 due to the upcoming state visit of the Sultan of Oman. The State Security Service of Kazakhstan stated that security measures will be in place, involving special state and law enforcement resources.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish International R&D Centers in Energy and AI
item.description: Kazakhstan will establish international research and development centers in the fields of energy and artificial intelligence. Three documents were signed at the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum to develop scientific and technological cooperation. Joint R&D centers with Chinese partners are planned at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University.

item.title: Sultan of Oman to Make State Visit to Kazakhstan
item.description: The Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, will pay a state visit to Kazakhstan on October 5-6 at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. High-level talks will focus on strengthening political dialogue and expanding trade, economic, investment, and cultural cooperation. The leaders will also attend a Kazakh-Omani business forum.

item.title: Astana Welcomes High-Level Guests: Sultan of Oman to Visit
item.description: Astana is preparing to host high-ranking visitors as the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said, is scheduled for a state visit on October 5-6. The visit will include high-level negotiations and a Kazakh-Omani business forum, focusing on strengthening bilateral ties and economic cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Oman Leaders to Hold Talks in Astana
item.description: The leaders of Kazakhstan and Oman will hold high-level negotiations in Astana on October 5-6. The discussions will focus on strengthening political dialogue and expanding trade, economic, investment, and cultural cooperation. Both heads of state will also attend the Kazakh-Omani business forum.

item.title: Yemen Conflict Displaces Over 200,000 People Amid Intensifying Fighting
item.description: Intensified fighting between Houthis and Yemeni government forces has displaced over 200,000 people. Displaced individuals, including vulnerable groups, are sheltering in tents under difficult conditions without humanitarian aid. The conflict has escalated significantly in recent weeks, raising regional concerns.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Mongolia Agree to Develop Trade and Transport Links
item.description: Kazakhstan and Mongolia have agreed to enhance cooperation in trade, economy, science, technology, and culture. Both sides emphasized the need to boost transport and logistics infrastructure to increase trade turnover. Discussions also included opening new air routes between the capitals.

item.title: Russia Expresses Concern Over Pakistani Airstrikes on Afghanistan; Envoy Stresses Regional Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Russian embassy voiced concern regarding civilian casualties from Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan. Meanwhile, Afghanistan's envoy in Moscow highlighted the importance of regional economic cooperation, dialogue, and mutual respect during a forum. He also discussed trade and investment with a Russian regional minister and addressed concerns of Afghan expatriates.

item.title: Man Wanted by Interpol Extradited from Georgia to Uzbekistan
item.description: A citizen accused of large-scale fraud has been extradited from Georgia to Uzbekistan, according to Interpol's National Central Bureau in Uzbekistan. The individual was internationally wanted for fraud under Article 168 of the Criminal Code. Following coordinated efforts between Interpol bureaus, the suspect was apprehended in Georgia and subsequently handed over to Uzbekistan.

item.title: President Trump States Iran is "Crushed," Discusses Future Actions
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump recently stated that Iran has been "crushed" and claimed the country abandoned nuclear weapons plans. Trump asserted he had set back Iran's nuclear program by several years. He also mentioned considering future actions against Iran, depending on whether they are pursued the "easy way or the hard way."

item.title: Fugitive Sought by Interpol Extradited to Uzbekistan from Georgia
item.description: An individual wanted internationally by Interpol has been extradited to Uzbekistan from Georgia. The suspect is believed to have committed fraud involving a very large sum of money. The extradition was facilitated through Interpol channels.

item.title: India and Pakistan Summon Diplomats Over Deadly Border Incident
item.description: India and Pakistan summoned each other's top diplomats following a border incident on October 2. New Delhi rejected Pakistan's claim that Indian forces killed two unarmed civilians, stating the individuals had illegally crossed into Indian territory and posed a security threat.

item.title: Kazakhstan Finishes Eighth at 2026 Asian Games with 84 Medals
item.description: The 2026 Asian Games concluded with Kazakhstan's equestrian team competing in Tokyo. The national team secured 84 medals overall: 12 gold, 24 silver, and 48 bronze, placing eighth among 46 participating nations. This performance marks a decline from their consistent top-five rankings in previous Games.

item.title: Afghanistan United Front Claims Killing Taliban Fighter in Helmand
item.description: The Afghanistan United Front claims responsibility for killing a Taliban fighter in Helmand province. The group stated on X that the operation occurred near Lashkar Gah. This follows a similar claim made the previous day regarding an incident in Kandahar. Anti-Taliban attacks have reportedly increased recently.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Requests Military Aid from Europe to Combat Houthis, Criticizes Western Security Contributions
item.description: Saudi Arabia has requested military assistance from European nations to counter the Houthis, criticizing Western countries for insufficient contributions to regional security. Riyadh emphasized that protecting trade routes is not solely the responsibility of the United States. The call highlights concerns over maritime security and the need for broader international cooperation.

item.title: Three Mobile Operators Fined in Kostanay for Exceeding Signal Levels in Prisons
item.description: Three mobile operators, 'Kar-Tel', 'Kcell', and 'Mobile Telecom-Service', have been fined in the Kostanay region for exceeding permitted radio signal levels within correctional facilities. This violation was discovered during a special inspection of the penal system. Previously, a prisoner was prosecuted for fraud committed via mobile phone.

item.title: Wealthy Russians Contributed Over $5.6 Billion to Russia's Budget for War Efforts
item.description: Wealthy individuals in Russia transferred over 471 billion rubles, exceeding $5.6 billion, to the state budget as 'voluntary contributions' for the war in 2026. This sum covers over 1% of the government's total expenditures. The initiative reportedly originated from a closed meeting between President Putin and businessmen, many of whom are under Western sanctions. Kremlin denies soliciting funds, stating a participant offered a large sum.

item.title: Russia Warns Foreign Nationals Against Traveling to Ukraine, Citing Risks
item.description: Russia has issued a warning advising foreign nationals against traveling to Ukraine. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that those who disregard the warning risk their lives and will be solely responsible for any consequences. The advisory highlights the dangers associated with travel to the conflict zone.

item.title: Kazakhstan Finishes Asian Games with 84 Medals, Ranking 11th
item.description: Kazakhstan concluded the Asian Games in Hangzhou with 84 medals, securing 11th place overall. This performance marked a three-place improvement from the previous games, with an increased number of gold medals. The team achieved several historic results in Olympic sports, including a silver medal in the mixed team judo event and a historic gold in taekwondo.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Mongolia to Increase Mutual Trade Volume Fivefold
item.description: Kazakhstan and Mongolia plan to boost their mutual trade volume five times. This agreement was reached during a meeting between Kazakh First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlibek Naliyev and Mongolian Deputy Prime Minister N. Nomtoybayar. Discussions covered trade, energy, digitalization, and culture, with a focus on transport links, including the new Astana-Ulaanbaatar flight.

item.title: Uzbek Official: Central Asia Emerging as Independent Center in Polycentric World
item.description: Akramjon Nematov, Deputy Director of the Institute for Strategic and Interregional Studies, stated that Central Asia is becoming an independent center of interaction in the emerging polycentric world. He participated in the 23rd 'Valdai' Club meeting in Istra, Russia, which discussed global development and transformations.

item.title: Yemeni Houthis Claim Attack on Aramco Facility in Riyadh
item.description: Yemeni Houthis announced on Saturday they attacked an Aramco facility in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia's capital. The military spokesperson stated ballistic missiles and drones were used. This follows reports of smoke and flames from an oil facility south of Riyadh. Saudi forces also conducted airstrikes on Sanaa.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Measures Against Spread of Dangerous Infectious Diseases
item.description: Uzbekistan has intensified measures to prevent the spread of highly dangerous infectious diseases. This update comes as part of a daily news digest released on October 3rd. Further details on specific actions taken were not provided in the source material.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Unified Ministry of Education and Science to Streamline Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a single Ministry of Education and Science, merging previous ministries for preschool, school, and higher education. The new ministry will oversee all educational institutions, set standards, and handle accreditation. The Presidential Administration and a special working group will develop the ministry's structure and strategy.

item.title: Uzbek Presidential Spokesperson Explains New Education System Reforms
item.description: Presidential spokesperson Sherzod Asadov detailed the reforms for Uzbekistan's education system, including the establishment of a unified Ministry of Education and Science. This ministry will manage all preschool, school, and higher education institutions. The Presidential Administration and a working group will design the ministry's structure and processes.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Enhance Road Quality Control, Contractors to Rectify Defects at Own Expense
item.description: Kazakhstan is strengthening road quality control, with contractors now required to fix defects at their own expense during the warranty period. First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlan Nalinbaev emphasized stricter oversight and accountability in road infrastructure development, aligning with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's focus on tangible results.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate convenes 20th plenary session in Tashkent, discusses construction sector corruption
item.description: The 20th plenary session of the Senate of Uzbekistan convened in Tashkent, addressing corruption and conflict of interest in the construction sector. Participants included government officials and media representatives. The session focused on improving risk assessment and transparency in public procurement within the Ministry of Construction.

item.title: Zafar Hoshimov to Lead New Working Group on Human Capital Development
item.description: A new working group is being established under the Presidential Administration to develop a national concept for human capital development and continuous education. Businessman Zafar Hoshimov will lead the group on a public basis. The group will include entrepreneurs, specialists, scientists, and international experts experienced in establishing educational institutions and creating effective systems.

item.title: Zafar Hoshimov to Lead Group Developing Human Capital Strategy Concept
item.description: A special working group is being formed under the Presidential Administration to develop a nationwide concept for human capital development and continuous education. Businessman Zafar Hoshimov will lead the group on a voluntary basis. The group will comprise entrepreneurs, specialists, scientists, and international experts experienced in establishing educational institutions and creating effective systems.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Discusses Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid with UN Official
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with UN Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo to discuss cooperation, humanitarian assistance, and the needs of Afghan returnees. They also addressed climate change, water issues, regional stability, and the importance of accurate information for balanced reporting. Concerns over civilian harm from Pakistani airstrikes were also raised.

item.title: Pakistan's Internal Political Crisis Escalation Discussed on Tahawol Program
item.description: The Tahawol program discussed the escalating internal political crisis in Pakistan. Other regional news included US-Iran mediation efforts, US sanctions on Iran's weapons procurement, a deadly airstrike in Helmand, and Afghanistan's groundwater warnings.

item.title: Obid Hakimov Appointed Deputy Head of Presidential Administration for Education Reform
item.description: Obid Hakimov has been appointed Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration for Education Reform and concurrently serves as Rector of the "New Uzbekistan" University. He previously advised on economic policy. Ilhom Sirojev, his predecessor, was appointed Deputy Minister of Preschool and School Education.

item.title: Uzbekistan Appoints New Deputy Head of Presidential Administration and Advisor
item.description: Obid Hakimov has been appointed Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration, while Kamoliddin Mardonov is now an advisor to the president. Hakimov will also continue as rector of the New Uzbekistan University. Mardonov previously served as the president's advisor on economic policy.

item.title: West Kazakhstan Region Restores Discounted Travel Rights for Teenagers
item.description: The Burly District Prosecutor's Office in West Kazakhstan Region identified violations affecting minors aged 16-17. They were previously denied discounted public transport fares. Following a prosecutor's appeal, the district maslikhat amended its decision, restoring a 50% fare reduction for these teenagers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Merges Education Ministries into Single Ministry of Education and Science
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has decreed the merger of the Ministry of Preschool and School Education with the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Innovations. The new unified Ministry of Education and Science aims to enhance the quality and efficiency of education and develop human capital. This reform seeks to create a cohesive system from preschool to higher education.
